// The command layer of the reach fixture. Two commands over one helper package:
// one that gates and one that does not, so every reach class the verdict
// distinguishes has a witness here rather than only in the repo, where a
// refactor could quietly remove the last example of one.
//
// A fixture, not compiled source — see ungated.go.txt for why .go.txt.

package rootpkg

import (
	"github.com/spf13/cobra"

	"example.com/fixture/helperpkg"
)

// Ungated reaches a spawn through TWO NAMED HOPS in another package. Nothing
// about it is gated, so every site it alone reaches must be flagged.
func Ungated() *cobra.Command {
	return &cobra.Command{
		Use: "ungated",
		RunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
			if err := helperpkg.HopOne(); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			return helperpkg.Shared()
		},
	}
}

// Gated acts on requireExecConsent's result, which is what makes it gating —
// the name alone is not enough, or doctor's display-only LaneConsented call
// would gate doctor.
func Gated() *cobra.Command {
	return &cobra.Command{
		Use: "gated",
		RunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
			if err := requireExecConsent(); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			if err := helperpkg.GatedOnly(); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			return helperpkg.Shared()
		},
	}
}

// Displaying reads a consent state and never acts on it. It must NOT gate:
// this is doctor.go's reportLaneConsent in miniature.
func Displaying() *cobra.Command {
	return &cobra.Command{
		Use: "displaying",
		RunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
			state, cerr := helperpkg.LaneConsented()
			println(state, cerr)
			return helperpkg.Displayed()
		},
	}
}

func requireExecConsent() error { return nil }
